# Refuse commits that credit anyone but toibawani.
#
# Two things went wrong in this repository's history and neither was caught by
# reading the log: 41 commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer naming an agent,
# and one commit was made as "apple <apple@apples-MacBook-Air.local>". The
# trailer is the easy one, because any tool that writes a commit message adds
# it; the identity is the quiet one, because a stray `git config` or a CI
# runner's default environment is enough to produce it.
#
# This hook runs at commit time, before the object exists, and exits non-zero
# so the commit never lands. scripts/commitAuthorship.js enforces the same
# rules in CI for commits that arrive by push or pull request.

msg_file="$1"
status=0

if [ -z "$msg_file" ] || [ ! -f "$msg_file" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: no message file given" >&2
	exit 1
fi

trailers=$(grep -in '^[[:space:]]*co-authored-by[[:space:]]*:' "$msg_file")
if [ -n "$trailers" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: refusing a Co-Authored-By trailer:" >&2
	echo "$trailers" | sed 's/^/  /' >&2
	echo "  Remove the line. Do not name an agent as an author of a commit." >&2
	status=1
fi

# `git var` resolves exactly the identity this commit will use, including
# GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL environment overrides, so this catches the
# case where the config is right and the environment is not.
author_ident=$(GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
author_name=${author_ident%% <*}
author_rest=${author_ident#*<}
author_email=${author_rest%%>*}

committer_ident=$(GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='@0 +0000' git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT 2>/dev/null)
committer_name=${committer_ident%% <*}
committer_rest=${committer_ident#*<}
committer_email=${committer_rest%%>*}

if [ "$author_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$author_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: author is '$author_name <$author_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2
	echo "  Fix with: git config user.name toibawani && git config user.email toibawani14@gmail.com" >&2
	status=1
fi

if [ "$committer_name" != "toibawani" ] || [ "$committer_email" != "toibawani14@gmail.com" ]; then
	echo "commit-msg: committer is '$committer_name <$committer_email>', not 'toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com>'" >&2

/*
 * Fails when a commit credits someone other than toibawani.
 *
 * The commit-msg hook stops this on the machine that is committing, which is
 * the only place it can be stopped cheaply. This script exists because a hook
 * is local configuration: a fresh clone, a CI runner, or a tool that passes
 * --no-verify can all produce a commit the hook never saw. Run against a
 * range, it answers the question the hook cannot answer after the fact.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/commitAuthorship.js <range>     e.g. origin/main..HEAD
 *   node scripts/commitAuthorship.js             checks HEAD itself
 *
 * Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 violation, 2 could not run.
 */

const { execFileSync } = require('child_process');

const NAME = 'toibawani';
const EMAIL = 'toibawani14@gmail.com';

function git(args) {
  return execFileSync('git', args, { encoding: 'utf8' });
}

function commitsIn(range) {
  // Record separator and field separator are chosen so a commit body cannot
  // forge a boundary: NUL never appears in a commit message field.
  const format = ['%H', '%an', '%ae', '%cn', '%ce', '%B'].join('%x00') + '%x1e';
  const out = git(['log', '--no-color', '--format=' + format, range]);
  return out
    .split('\x1e')
    .map((chunk) => chunk.replace(/^\n/, ''))
    .filter((chunk) => chunk.length > 0)
    .map((chunk) => {
      const [hash, an, ae, cn, ce, body] = chunk.split('\x00');
      return { hash, author: { name: an, email: ae }, committer: { name: cn, email: ce }, body: body || '' };
    });
}

function trailerLines(body) {
  return body
    .split('\n')
    .map((line, index) => ({ line: line.trim(), number: index + 1 }))
    .filter((entry) => /^co-authored-by\s*:/i.test(entry.line));
}

function main() {
  const range = process.argv[2] || 'HEAD';
  let commits;
  try {
    commits = commitsIn(range);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`commit-authorship: could not read commits in "${range}": ${error.message.trim()}`);
    process.exit(2);
  }

  if (commits.length === 0) {
    console.error(`commit-authorship: no commits in "${range}"`);
    process.exit(2);
  }

  const problems = [];
  for (const commit of commits) {
    if (commit.author.name !== NAME || commit.author.email !== EMAIL) {
      problems.push(
        `${commit.hash.slice(0, 7)} author is "${commit.author.name} <${commit.author.email}>"`
      );
    }
    if (commit.committer.name !== NAME || commit.committer.email !== EMAIL) {
      problems.push(
        `${commit.hash.slice(0, 7)} committer is "${commit.committer.name} <${commit.committer.email}>"`
      );
    }
    for (const trailer of trailerLines(commit.body)) {
      problems.push(`${commit.hash.slice(0, 7)} message line ${trailer.number}: ${trailer.line}`);
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error(`commit-authorship: ${problems.length} problem(s) in ${commits.length} commit(s) (${range})`);
    for (const problem of problems) console.error(`  ${problem}`);
    console.error('Commits must be authored and committed by toibawani <toibawani14@gmail.com> with no Co-Authored-By trailer.');
    process.exit(1);
  }

  console.log(`commit-authorship: ${commits.length} commit(s) in ${range} are all toibawani <${EMAIL}> and carry no credit trailers`);
}

main();

/**
 * Keeps Tab inside a dialog.
 *
 * Four overlays in this app declare role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" and
 * then let Tab walk straight out of them into the page behind. aria-modal tells
 * a screen reader the rest of the page is unavailable, so leaving the keyboard

 * user can end up typing into a form they cannot see.

 * The handler sits on the dialog element and only acts on Tab. When focus is on
 * the last control it wraps to the first, and Shift+Tab on the first wraps to
 * the last. Everything else is left alone, so the browser still owns ordinary
 * tab order inside the dialog.
 *
 * jsdom has no layout, so this deliberately does not filter controls by
 * visibility: offsetParent is null for everything there, and a visibility test
 * would make the trap look implemented in tests and do nothing in a browser.
 * The CSS is responsible for hiding what should not be reachable, and the
 * dialogs here do not render hidden controls.
 */
const FOCUSABLE = [
  'a[href]',
  'button:not([disabled])',
  'input:not([disabled])',
  'select:not([disabled])',
  'textarea:not([disabled])',
  '[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])',
].join(',');

export default function useFocusTrap(ref, active = true) {
  useEffect(() => {
    const node = ref.current;
    if (!active || !node) return undefined;

    const handleKeyDown = (event) => {
      if (event.key !== 'Tab') return;

      const controls = Array.from(node.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE)).filter(
        (element) => element.getAttribute('aria-hidden') !== 'true'
      );
      if (controls.length === 0) return;

      const first = controls[0];
      const last = controls[controls.length - 1];
      const current = document.activeElement;

      if (event.shiftKey && (current === first || !node.contains(current))) {
        event.preventDefault();
        last.focus();
      } else if (!event.shiftKey && (current === last || !node.contains(current))) {
        event.preventDefault();
        first.focus();
      }
    };

    node.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);
    return () => node.removeEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);
  }, [ref, active]);
}
